## apiome primitives {#primitives}

Import a tenant's primitives in bulk.

```text
apiome primitives [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Subcommands: [`import`](#primitives-import).

## apiome primitives import {#primitives-import}

Import primitives from a file (POST /v1/primitives/{tenant}/import).

The file holds one primitive or an array of them: name, base (a JSON Schema type) and any schema keyword such as pattern or examples — or name and schema, as `types list --json` prints.

Every row is checked here first, then reviewed by the server; nothing is written before you confirm, or without --yes when there is no terminal.

A row that fails stops the import with exit 7, unless --continue-on-error.

```text
apiome primitives import [OPTIONS] [FILE]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | text |  | JSON or YAML file of primitives; omit or pass - to read stdin. |

**Options**

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  |  | Show what would be imported, and the conflicts, without writing. |
| `--update` | flag |  |  | Overwrite an existing primitive with the same name. |
| `--skip-conflicts` | flag |  |  | Leave an existing primitive with the same name alone (the default). |
| `--yes`, `-y` | flag |  |  | Import without asking. Required when there is no terminal. |
| `--continue-on-error` | flag |  |  | Import the rows that are fine when others fail, and exit 0. |
| `--report` | path |  |  | Write a JSON report with one entry per row. |
